title: The badge in two places
objectives: Construct a parenthesized OR inside an event-type boundary.
Filter failure actions without equating failure with malicious intent.
story: MIDNIGHT AT MERIDIAN / CHAPTER 2 — The fictional show account appears in a sign-in story and an account-management story. Mira asks whether it was doing something or having something done to it. Learn the principal/target distinction, then keep Boolean alternatives inside a clear boundary.

teaching.heading: Actor is not a job title
teaching.text: Principal describes an actor in an event. Target describes the affected or referenced thing. Neither means CEO, engineer or administrator. Your source's mapping decides what the fields contain.

teaching.heading: AND narrows; OR offers alternatives
teaching.text: A AND B requires both. A OR B permits either. To ask for login events involving either identity role, keep the identity alternatives inside parentheses.

teaching.heading: Read the whole question
teaching.text: Category AND (principal OR target) keeps both branches inside the login category. Category AND principal OR target can let the final branch escape that category.

teaching.heading: The query is a lead
teaching.text: A failure record does not prove an attack. Use context and chronology privately. The course only checks whether the query asks its stated question.

challenges.title: Follow either identity role
challenges.prompt: Select only USER_LOGIN events in which [USER] appears in principal.user.userid OR target.user.userid. Preserve the event-type requirement for both branches. Use exact case-sensitive strings and return event rows.
hints: The category must constrain every identity branch.
Place the two identity alternatives inside parentheses, then AND that group with USER_LOGIN.

methodQuestions.prompt: Why are the identity alternatives grouped?

options.label: To make the query look shorter
To keep both alternatives inside the USER_LOGIN scope
To automatically join two different events

methodQuestions.rationale: The group expresses alternatives within one event filter. It does not perform a multi-event join.

methodQuestions.prompt: A username appears in target. What can you infer?

options.label: It is necessarily the actor responsible
Its role must be interpreted using the event and parser mapping

methodQuestions.rationale: Field role and event context matter; names alone do not establish causality.

executeSteps: Check how both identity roles are populated in an authorized login source.
Replace the synthetic user only inside SecOps and run with an approved range.
Compare a few relevant event details privately, checking what principal and target mean.
If no rows return, check mapping and identity case before assuming absence.
challenges.debrief: Describe privately how a missing parenthesis would change scope. The app will demonstrate a synthetic counterexample, never a real event.

mission.beat: The fictional badge card may appear as actor or target. Keep the whole question inside the login category.

explanation.meaning: The account recorded in the actor role specified by this query.
The account in the affected or referenced role. Check source meaning privately.
Permit either identity field to match the same course symbol.
Require the login category for both alternatives. Parentheses keep that boundary intact.

mission.remember: OR opens alternatives. Parentheses keep the doorframe.
mission.caseUpdate: Case card unlocked: you can search both identity roles without admitting unrelated categories.

challenges.title: Keep the failure question focused
challenges.prompt: Select USER_LOGIN events with security_result.action = FAIL and principal.user.userid exactly [USER]. No target-role OR is requested in this challenge. Return event rows.
hints: Keep category and exact actor identity, then add the documented action filter.
Use security_result.action = "FAIL" as another required condition.

methodQuestions.prompt: Do failed login records prove an attack?

options.label: No; inspect context and source normalization before forming an incident conclusion
Only if the query contains three fields

methodQuestions.rationale: A failure action is an observation. Frequency, source, baseline, and surrounding activity determine what it might mean.

methodQuestions.prompt: The source records a different failure representation. What next?

options.label: Rename FAIL to an invented enum
Verify normalization and adapt the private workplace search if appropriate
Send the raw failure log to the course

methodQuestions.rationale: Use actual supported fields and values from the source mapping; do not invent enum values.

executeSteps: Privately confirm that the selected source populates security_result.action and the intended userid role.
Replace [USER] only in SecOps, run, and inspect action values in event details.
Keep any interpretation in approved workplace notes.
An empty result is a legitimate outcome after checking mapping and range.
challenges.debrief: Separate the observation 'matched a failure action' from the hypothesis 'an attack is occurring'.

mission.beat: Mira narrows the next fictional question to failures for the actor account. This mission does not ask for a target-role alternative.

explanation.meaning: Require the stated actor account, using only the training symbol here.
All three requirements must hold together.

mission.remember: A narrow question needs every boundary attached.
mission.caseUpdate: Case card unlocked: the fictional account lead is scoped. Next, pivot to the workstation.
